hints: Look first at the two easy lines in this graph. Which line starts highest and falls, and which line starts near zero and rises to a high plateau?

Remember the enzyme cycle $E + S \rightarrow ES \rightarrow E + P$. Free enzyme is used up to make ES at the start, then released again when substrate runs out, so what up-down-up shape should it have?
walkthrough:
**Spot substrate and product first**

Think simply. Substrate is used up, so its concentration starts high and falls steadily. Product is made, so it starts at zero and rises to a plateau.

That means line C is substrate and line A is product.

**Think about what happens to free enzyme**

At time zero, no substrate has bound yet, so all enzyme active sites are empty. Free enzyme concentration starts at its maximum.

Then the reaction is:
$$E + S \rightarrow ES \rightarrow E + P$$

**Match the dip and recovery to line B**

As soon as substrate is added, free enzyme quickly binds it, so free enzyme falls sharply. Later, as substrate (line C) runs out, less ES can form and more enzyme is released empty again, so free enzyme rises back up.

Only line B shows this fall then rise to a low steady level. That is enzymes with empty active sites.

options.A: Line A starts near zero and rises to a high plateau, which is the product accumulating, not free enzyme.
options.B: Line B falls quickly as empty enzymes bind substrate to form ES, then rises again as ES breaks down and releases free enzyme when substrate is low.
options.C: Line C starts highest and falls steadily, which is the substrate being used up, not the enzyme.
options.D: Line D stays very low, rising slightly then falling, which is the short-lived enzyme-substrate complex, not free enzyme.
